subChunks.title: Self-paced orientation: Foundation
subChunks.hookHtml: This orientation turns a large subject into a manageable plan: learn the language first, then build explanations layer by layer.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core lesson

Psychology rewards steady sequencing. In this phase you build the vocabulary, biological background, cognitive models, and basic research habits that later topics depend on.

Key ideas

  • Treat the phase as a map, not a race.
  • Keep a learning journal with definitions, examples, and uncertainties.
  • Use retrieval practice after each module before starting the next.

How to study this module

Read the lesson once, then close it. Try to rebuild the explanation in your own words before you check the notes. Psychology becomes useful when you can move between definition, example, evidence, and limitation.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Guided lesson: what to write

Open your notes and write the following. Each line has a purpose: it turns the idea into something you can retrieve and use later.

  1. Step 1: Write the four Foundation pathway names in order.
  2. Step 2: Under each pathway, write one reason it must come before advanced topics.
  3. Step 3: Circle the pathway you expect to find hardest and write a review plan for it.

Why you are writing it

This makes the route visible and turns self-paced study into a sequence of deliberate choices.
